newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Polish 52-wk bill yield dip seen smaller.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Polish 52-wk bill yield dip seen smaller.

text.p: Banks revised upwards their forecasts for the average yield on Poland's benchmark 52-week T-bill and expect it to fall to 19.23 percent by the end of 1996, a Reuters poll of the country's 25 largest banks showed.
Last month, banks saw the benchmark yield falling to 18.85 percent by year-end. At the last primary auction, the benchmark yield stood at 19.50 percent.
The average forecast is the mean of banks' forecasts ranging from 18.00 to 19.60 percent. @
By the end of this month, the yield is seen rising to an average of 19.52 percent, with a range from 19.40 to 19.90 percent.
In November 1997, the yield was seen falling further to an average of 17.19 percent. Forecasts ranged from 16.00 to 19.00 percent.
The average yield on the 13-week T-bill is seen falling to 18.39 percent by year-end from 18.60 percent at the last primary auction, the poll showed.
The 13-week T-bill yield forecast is a mean average of banks' predictions ranging from 17.50 percent to 19.00 percent.
On average, the yield is seen at 18.60 percent at the end of this month with a 18.45 percent to 19.45 percent range but is expected to fall to 16.69 percent in November 1997.
Forecasts for November 1997 ranged from 15.00 to 18.10 percent.
